clue.text: No longer piece of music

definitions.meaning: the abbreviation No written out at full, longer length
a song or item in a performance, as in a musical's big show-stopper

explanation.walkthrough: 'No longer' looks like 'not any more', but it asks for the abbreviation No spelt out in full.
explanation.definitionFit: A song in a show is called a number, and No is the standard abbreviation of that word.

clue.text: Dance venue near Bath impressing couple from Clifton

parts.note: nigh is an old word for near

indicators.note: the bath presses around the letters, which end up inside it

parts.note: a tub is a bath

indicators.note: the first two letters of the place name are taken

explanation.surface: A disco near the city of Bath draws a couple from Clifton, a district of Bristol.
explanation.walkthrough: Bath and Clifton are real West Country places, a city and a Bristol suburb, so they read as geography rather than a tub and two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightclub is a late-night venue where people go dancing.

clue.text: What butcher may be doing in camp?

definitions.meaning: a butcher grinds meat into small pieces

explanation.walkthrough: 'camp' looks like a place a butcher may be working, but it is the adjective for affected manners.
explanation.definitionFit: Chopping meat finely is the butcher's sense; walking with dainty affected steps is the camp sense.

clue.text: Catch butty that's cut up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read from bottom to top, backwards
the word has its final letter cut off

parts.note: butty is northern English and Welsh dialect for a mate or partner

explanation.surface: A sandwich, or butty in British slang, has been sliced up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butty' wants to be the British word for a sandwich; here it is the dialect word for a mate. 'cut' drops the last R of PARTNER, leaving PARTNE, which 'up' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: To trap someone is to catch them out, often by a trick.

clue.text: Men died protecting tea trees here

indicators.note: the outer pieces surround and shield the tea, so it sits inside them

parts.note: OR, other ranks, is the crossword term for soldiers who are not officers
d. is the abbreviation for died in genealogies
char is British slang for tea, from the Chinese cha

explanation.surface: Soldiers who died guarding a tea plantation.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchard is a plot planted with fruit trees, so it is the place where such trees grow.

clue.text: Old hands finish off without hard paint

indicators.note: in its old sense of outside, the crew word goes around the H
the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: hands are workers, the crew of a ship
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Elderly workers finish without hard paint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' reads as 'lacking', but here it means outside: CRE, from CREW with its end gone, sits around H.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is an earthy yellow-brown pigment used in paint.

clue.text: Not worried about a heartless judge

parts.note: c., circa, is Latin for about
taken as written

indicators.note: the middle letter of the word is removed

parts.note: a referee judges a game

explanation.surface: Someone is unbothered about a cruel judge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes the central E from REFEREE, leaving REFREE.
explanation.definitionFit: Carefree means free from anxiety, untroubled.

clue.text: Exercise in a bar got going

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the exercise word goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: a rod is a bar of metal or wood
to exercise a right is to use it

explanation.surface: A workout at the gym bar gets someone moving.
explanation.definitionFit: Aroused means stirred into action, woken or got going.

clue.text: Small daughters getting stuck into homework?

indicators.note: the daughters are put inside the other piece

parts.note: DIY, do-it-yourself, is work done on the home, a pun on homework
d is the abbreviation for daughter, so two daughters are DD

explanation.surface: Little girls get down to their homework.
explanation.walkthrough: DIDDY is British informal for small or tiny.
explanation.definitionFit: Diddy is British slang for something tiny or little.

clue.text: Former police leave a unit oddly neglected

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters are skipped, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: Ex-police officers abandon a unit in a strange way.
explanation.definitionFit: Ci-devant is French for formerly, used in English for someone who was once something.

clue.text: See about home for Geordie's mammal

indicators.note: one piece goes around the other, enclosing it

parts.note: to get something is to see or understand it
a Geordie is a native of Tyneside, in the North East of England, abbreviated NE

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to look into a creature that lives in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: The genet is a small spotted carnivore related to the civets, a kind of mammal.

clue.text: Novelist is joining crowd outside court

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the crowd word sits around the court word, enclosing it

parts.note: a herd is a crowd or throng
to court someone is to woo them

explanation.surface: A writer joins a throng gathered outside a law court.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Isherwood was an English writer of novels, best known for Goodbye to Berlin.

clue.text: Islanders getting wet in a sea that's rough

indicators.note: rough sea churns things up, so these letters are tossed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: People on an island get soaked in a choppy sea.
explanation.definitionFit: People from Taiwan, an island off the coast of China, are islanders.

clue.text: Queer poem back to front, backward in coming forward

indicators.note: the poem's title is to be read in reverse order

parts.note: If is Kipling's famous poem
a British idiom for timid or bashful

explanation.surface: An odd poem written in reverse by someone too modest to put themselves forward.
explanation.definitionFit: Queer in its old sense of strange or suspicious matches something that seems dubious or odd.

clue.text: Record sleeve's last in box

parts.note: a log is a written record, like a ship's log

indicators.note: the final letter of the word for the record cover is taken

explanation.surface: A record sleeve ends up last in a storage box.
explanation.definitionFit: A loge is a box in a theatre, a private compartment for spectators.

clue.text: Miller, say, stopped songs being heard

indicators.note: the phrase is to be spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: banned means stopped or forbidden, and lieder are German art songs

explanation.surface: Someone called Miller has had their songs banned from being heard.
explanation.definitionFit: Glenn Miller led a famous wartime big band, an example of a leader of a dance orchestra.

clue.text: Despite appearances, a profoundly comforting filler

definitions.meaning: a thick layer of soft feathers in a quilt, playfully read

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is playful: down is the soft feather filling of quilts, and a deep layer of it is very comforting.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep down means at heart, whatever things look like; down is also quilt filling.

clue.text: Bottom line — get 21 again?

parts.note: the rear is the bottom or backside
a range is a line, as of mountains

explanation.surface: The final verdict is to get the thing working again.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 is the 21-down answer, IN ORDER; getting things in order again is to rearrange them. The held text dropped the 1.
explanation.definitionFit: To put something in order a second time is to rearrange it.

clue.text: Cowboy with right point of view heading for ranch

parts.note: an angle is a viewpoint or slant

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A cowboy with the right attitude heads towards the ranch.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrangler is a ranch hand who herds horses, a cowboy in the American West.

clue.text: Watcher of Balthasar's back in Much Ado

indicators.note: the end letter of the name is placed inside the other phrase

parts.note: a big bother is much ado, a great fuss

indicators.note: the rearmost letter of the name is taken

explanation.surface: Balthasar, a character in Shakespeare's Much Ado About Nothing, is watched from behind.
explanation.walkthrough: Balthasar is a singer in Much Ado About Nothing, which makes the play title look like a reference rather than a phrase meaning a great fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: Orwell's all-seeing ruler of Nineteen Eighty-Four is the ever-present watcher of the citizens.

clue.text: Vertiginous rider's accelerator?

parts.note: a dizzy word plus up makes the call a horseman gives to speed a horse

explanation.walkthrough: The rider is on horseback, and the accelerator is the call to go faster; the first part also means dizzy.
explanation.definitionFit: Riders call to their horses to make them go or speed up with this cry.

clue.text: Girl working in auction houses

indicators.note: the words hold the name inside them, as a house holds its occupants

explanation.surface: A young woman is employed at an auction house.
explanation.definitionFit: Gina is a woman's given name, so it stands for any girl.

clue.text: Working as a monk?

definitions.meaning: belonging to a religious community such as the Benedictines

explanation.walkthrough: A monk belongs to a religious order, so he is literally in one.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that functions is in good order; a monk is a member of a religious order.

clue.text: Greeting, I'm sorry to say, upset a mourner initially

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned over, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: alas expresses regret
taken as written

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Someone regretfully says hello to a grieving person.
explanation.definitionFit: Salaam is an Arabic greeting meaning peace, with a low bow.

clue.text: Dizzy blondes trimmed waterproof material

indicators.note: a dizzy head spins, so the letters are whirled into a new order
the word has its two ends cut off

explanation.surface: Giddy fair-haired women had their hair cut and wear rainproof clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trimmed' cuts B and S from 'blondes', leaving LONDE, which 'Dizzy' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Loden is a thick water-resistant woollen cloth from the Tyrol, used for coats.

clue.text: Go and cut Whitman's grass

indicators.note: the final letter of the title word is cut off

parts.note: Walt Whitman's poetry collection is Leaves of Grass

explanation.surface: Someone goes off to mow Whitman's lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' looks like mowing the grass, but it removes the S from LEAVES.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave is to go away or depart.

clue.text: Try to identify replacement for Challenger

definitions.meaning: the space shuttle built after the loss of Challenger in 1986

explanation.walkthrough: 'Challenger' looks like a contender in a contest, but it is the NASA space shuttle lost in 1986; its successor shuttle bore this name.
explanation.definitionFit: An attempt is an endeavour, and Endeavour was the orbiter NASA built to replace the lost shuttle.

clue.text: Distinctive character first seen in Edward Thomas

indicators.note: the opening letter of the name is taken

parts.note: Thos is the old abbreviation of the name Thomas

explanation.surface: A special quality is first noticed in the poet Edward Thomas.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethos is the characteristic spirit of a person, group or culture.

clue.text: Handy wool woven indiscriminately

indicators.note: weaving interlaces strands, so these letters are worked into a new pattern

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Useful wool knitted together in a careless way.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something any old how means doing it carelessly, without method or choice.

clue.text: Extra depth at first in a river

indicators.note: the initial letter goes inside the other two pieces

parts.note: taken as written
the Don is a river in Russia, and in Yorkshire and Scotland

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Extra depth is found at the start of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: An add-on is something extra attached to the main item.

clue.text: One boarding train almost passes on

indicators.note: a passenger boarding goes inside the vehicle
the word loses its last letter

parts.note: an express is a fast train
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A passenger gets on a train that has nearly gone past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts the final S from EXPRESS, giving EXPRES, which takes I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass on is a euphemism for dying, and to expire also means to die.

clue.text: Say corps in retreat is to break cover

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: eg, for example, means say
REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a corps of the British Army

explanation.surface: An army unit in retreat must come out from hiding.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming out of hiding is to emerge, to appear from concealment.
